findings.rule: Assumption 6 (within-tick double-assignment guard) vs work-items AC lines 92, 112, 114
findings.detail: The pending-offer exclusion (exclude drivers who are DriverId of an Assigned order in the fleet) is the SOLE guard against assigning one Free driver to two competing New orders in a single tick. The work-items doc is self-contradictory: line 114 correctly calls it the 'sole guard' relying on A's commit being visible when B's scope re-queries drivers, but WI-2 step 5 (line 92) and AC line 112 soften it to 'Optionally exclude' / 'Consider excluding.' The trap is PLACEMENT: a developer could implement this exclusion in the SCAN phase (cross-tenant, computed once before any assign) rather than inside each per-order scope. A scan-phase exclusion is stale for order B (order A was not yet Assigned at scan time), so the within-tick guard silently fails and the same driver receives two simultaneous offers. ApplyAssign leaves the driver Free (verified), so nothing else prevents the double offer.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the pending-offer exclusion (1) MANDATORY not optional; (2) queried INSIDE each per-order fresh scope (so prior same-tick commits by earlier orders are visible in the tenant-filtered reads); (3) unioned into the SINGLE excludedDriverIds set passed to NearestDriverSelector.SelectNearest (WI-1's selector takes exactly one IReadOnlySet<Guid>). Unify: excludedDriverIds = declined/timeout driver ids UNION (driver ids of orders currently Status==Assigned in this fleet). Keep the RunTick_TwoNewOrdersOneEligibleDriver_AssignsExactlyOne test as the backstop.

findings.detail: The SCAN-phase projection is under-specified. AC line 108 lists (OrderId, FleetId, PickupLat, PickupLng) plus per-fleet settings, but the in-memory filters also need CreatedAt (for 'CreatedAt + AutoDispatchAfterSeconds <= now') and ScheduledAt (for '(ScheduledAt == null || ScheduledAt <= now)'). OfferTimeoutJob projects AssignedAt for exactly this in-memory-arithmetic reason.
findings.suggested_fix: Add CreatedAt and ScheduledAt to the scan projection tuple; filter/compare in memory (mirror OfferTimeoutJob) to avoid EF DateTimeOffset-arithmetic translation issues.

findings.detail: Common/ is permitted 'only when reused by 2+ features.' NearestDriverSelector (Common/Dispatch/) has a single consumer (AutoDispatchJob). Placement is defensible on pure-testable-decision-module grounds (DI-free/I-O-free like HaversineDistance, enabling fast unit tests before the job's Testcontainers tests). Observed and justified, not a blocker.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep Common/Dispatch/ placement but record it in WI-1 notes as a conscious single-consumer exception mirroring the HaversineDistance pure-helper precedent, so a future reviewer does not flag it.

verified_not_findings.detail: Exclusion-set completeness (highest-risk) CORRECT. Only Assigned->New transitions are ApplyDecline and ApplyTimeout; both write the driver id into the event payload. ApplyAssign's Assigned event carries NULL payload and ApplyReassign is Assigned->Assigned. Deriving the exclusion set from Declined+Timeout payloads is a complete record of every driver already tried — no infinite re-offer loop.

OrderStateMachine.ApplyAssign accepts Actor.System (assign permitted for dispatcher OR system; AllowedFor grants Assign to System from New). Using OrderTransition.Assign + Actor.System is correct — mirrors OfferTimeoutJob's Timeout+Actor.System.

Concurrency handling returns results not exceptions. OrderService.TransitionAsync catches DbUpdateConcurrencyException -> TransitionResult.Failure(StaleVersion); IllegalTransition is a normal failure result. Both are IsSuccess==false the job checks — no exception surfaces.

ScheduledAt guard matches CreateOrderEndpoint: a future-ScheduledAt order is persisted Status=New immediately with no hold, so the (ScheduledAt==null||ScheduledAt<=now) guard is necessary to avoid auto-assigning a tomorrow ride now.

Job-pattern fidelity to OfferTimeoutJob confirmed (BackgroundService, IServiceScopeFactory+TimeProvider+ILogger ctor, thin PeriodicTimer(5s) ExecuteAsync->RunTickAsync, IgnoreQueryFilters+AsNoTracking scan, per-order fresh scope + concrete CurrentTenant.FleetId + OrderService, (int?)-cast settings guard). Missing-settings-row -> SKIP is a correct opt-in delta.

Eligibility inputs available and selector pure. Driver exposes Status/CurrentVehicleId/LastLat/LastLng/LastPositionAt; DriverStatus={Offline,Free,EnRoute,Busy} (Free sole eligible); HaversineDistance.Meters signature matches; StalePositionJob.StaleThreshold=5min. WI-1 SelectNearest DI-free/I-O-free.
Tenant isolation designed in + tested (per-order scope sets CurrentTenant.FleetId; EF query filter enforces isolation; RunTick_TenantIsolation_FleetBOrderUnaffected present).

Logging conforms: Information on assign OrderId/DriverId/FleetId (no PII), Debug no-eligible-driver with Reason, LogWarning per-order exception, LogError on unhandled tick. Job never sets order.Status and never publishes (OrderService owns event/Version/commit/broadcast).
DI registration correct: AddHostedService<AutoDispatchJob>() in JobsServiceExtensions.AddJobs alongside other jobs; gated per-fleet by FleetSettings.AutoDispatchEnabled, no global kill-switch needed.

Topology acyclic (WI-1 depends_on [], WI-2 depends_on [WI-1]); unit tests precede Testcontainers tests; all 8 spec test cases + 6 ACs map to WI test_cases; no new DTO/DbSet/AutoMapper — no architecture-ban violations.
